meta.title: Curated Cell Ontology (CL) terms for flow cytometry populations in human blood, PBMC and lymphoid tissue
meta.crossCheck: EBI OLS4 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/cl) served the same release (2026-06-08) on 2026-10-03. All terms were checked against OLS4: every label and definition matched and none is obsolete; OLS4 synonym lists differ only by non-exact synonyms.
meta.attribution: Contains text definitions, labels and synonyms from the Cell Ontology (release 2026-06-08), CC BY 4.0. Cite: Tan SZK et al. The Cell Ontology in the age of single-cell omics. Scientific Data 13 (2026). doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07173-8 (citation as given in the CL GitHub README; DOI verified via Crossref).
method: Terms selected by hand; all fields extracted programmatically from cl.obo.
synonyms: EXACT-scope synonyms only (RELATED/BROAD/NARROW omitted; OLS4 lists all scopes together).
clComment: the term's rdfs:comment, verbatim (CC BY 4.0), when present.

parents: nearest is_a ancestors (including is_a links that CL marks as inferred) that are in this curated set; if none, the direct CL is_a parents (see parentsNote). clIsA lists the direct CL is_a parents.

markers / markerAxioms: from intersection_of lines (the OWL equivalentClass logical definition; axiom="equivalentClass") and relationship lines (subClassOf restrictions; axiom="subClassOf"); "both" if the restriction appears in both.

Relation -> state: RO:0002104 has plasma membrane part -> "+"; CL:4030046 lacks_plasma_membrane_part -> "-"; RO:0015015 has high plasma membrane amount -> "high"; RO:0015016 has low plasma membrane amount -> "low"; BFO:0000051 has part (intracellular proteins and MHC-II) -> "+" with intracellular=true for transcription factors.
Only marker fillers (PR proteins; GO immunoglobulin, TCR and MHC-II complexes) are kept; morphology, function (GO process) and location restrictions are omitted.
inheritedMarkers: marker axioms of all CL is_a ancestors (whether or not in this set), with the source term; the nearest ancestor wins and the term's own axioms override.
Caveat: the OBO serialization carries only axioms expressible in OBO; complex OWL axioms (nested expressions, general class axioms) are not visible here.
practice: the conventional flow phenotype where CL axioms are silent, incomplete or use markers not on typical panels, with a citation. Practice phenotypes are suggestions, not CL content.

Nat Rev Immunol 12(3):191-200 (2012). doi:10.1038/nri3158; PMID 22343568; PMCID PMC3409649 (verified via Crossref and PMC ID converter; phenotypes read from the PMC full text).

CD56.note: Generic PR:000001024 in most terms; human-specific PR:P13591 in CL:4052055.

CD8.note: PR:000025402 is the CD8 alpha-beta co-receptor complex; CL uses it for alpha-beta T cell terms.

Ly6G.note: Mouse marker; appears only in CL lineage-negative definitions.

MHC-II.note: GO cellular component (MHC class II protein complex); HLA-DR antibodies are the usual surrogate. Distinct from HLA-DR (PR:000002015, HLA-DRA).

TCR.note: GO cellular component (T cell receptor complex). In practice CD3 is the surface surrogate (Maecker et al. 2012).

TCRgd.note: GO cellular component (gamma-delta TCR complex); measured with anti-TCRgd antibodies.

TER-119.note: Mouse marker; appears only in CL lineage-negative definitions.

TRAV1-2.note: TCR V alpha 7.2 (antibody clone 3C10 in OMIP-101).

terms.label: hematopoietic cell
terms.definition: A cell of a hematopoietic lineage.
terms.parentsNote: nearest CL ancestors (none in curated set)

terms.label: leukocyte
terms.definition: An achromatic cell of the myeloid or lymphoid lineages capable of ameboid movement, found in blood or other tissue.

practice.comment: Leukocytes are selected as CD45+ (CD45 vs SSC) after singlet/viability gates.

terms.label: mononuclear leukocyte
terms.definition: A leukocyte with a single non-segmented nucleus in the mature form.
terms.notes: CL lists 'peripheral blood mononuclear cell' as a NARROW synonym here; use CL:2000001 for PBMC.

terms.label: peripheral blood mononuclear cell
terms.definition: A leukocyte with a single non-segmented nucleus in the mature form found in the circulatory pool of blood.

practice.comment: Lymphocytes plus monocytes gated on FSC-A vs SSC-A from CD45+ events. In PBMC preparations this is the default root population.

terms.label: erythrocyte
terms.definition: A red blood cell. In mammals, mature erythrocytes are biconcave disks containing hemoglobin whose function is to transport oxygen.

practice.comment: Not gated positively in these OMIPs; excluded by lysis or by the CD45+ leukocyte gate. Useful as an exclusion label only.

terms.notes: Exclusion label. Logical definition: lacks CD71 and ribosomes, biconcave.

terms.label: platelet
terms.definition: A non-nucleated disk-shaped cell formed by extrusion from megakaryocytes, found in the blood of all mammals, and mainly involved in blood coagulation.
terms.clComment: Platelets are reportedly CCR1-positive, CCR2-negative, CCR3-positive, CCR4-positive, CCR5-negative, CCR6-negative, CCR7-negative, CCR8-negative, CCR9-negative, CCR10-negative, CD16-positive, CD23-positive, CD32-positive, CD40-positive, CD41-positive CD42-positive, CD61-positive, CD62P-positive, CD64-positive, CD89-positive, CD102-positive, CD147-positive (activated platelets), CD154-positive (activated platelets), CD162-positive, CD209, CD282-positive, CD284-positive, CD289-positive, CD181-negative, CD182-negative, CD183-negative, CD184-positive, CLEC2-positive, GPVI-positive, JAMC-positive, PAR1-positive, PAR2-negative, PAR3-positive, PAR4-positive, TSP1-positive, and TXA2R-positive. Platelets can reportedly produce CCL2, CCL3, CCL5, CCL7, CCL17, CD40L, CXCL1, CXCL4, CXCL4L1, CXCL5, CXCL7, CXCL8, CXCL12, EGF, factor V, factor VII, factor XI, factor XIII, bFGF, histamine, IGF-1, IL-1beta, PAI-1, PDGF, plasminogen, protein S, serotonin, TGF-beta, TFPI, VEGF, and vWF.

practice.comment: Not gated positively in these OMIPs; excluded by the CD45+ leukocyte and scatter gates. Exclusion label only.

terms.notes: Exclusion label. No marker axioms in CL.

terms.label: hematopoietic precursor cell
terms.definition: Any hematopoietic cell that is a precursor of some other hematopoietic cell type.

terms.label: hematopoietic stem cell
terms.definition: A stem cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop, including blood cells and cells of the immune system. Hematopoietic stem cells lack cell markers of effector cells (lin-negative). Lin-negative is defined by lacking one or more of the following cell surface markers: CD2, CD3 epsilon, CD4, CD5 ,CD8 alpha chain, CD11b, CD14, CD19, CD20, CD56, ly6G, ter119.
terms.clComment: Markers differ between species, and two sets of markers have been described for mice. HSCs are reportedly CD34-positive, CD45-positive, CD48-negative, CD150-positive, CD133-positive, and CD244-negative.
terms.notes: Generic HSC; lineage-negative defined by many lacks_plasma_membrane_part axioms (including mouse markers Ly6G and TER-119). For a CD34+ gate without CD38, CL:0008001 (hematopoietic precursor cell) is the safer suggestion.

terms.label: CD34-positive, CD38-negative hematopoietic stem cell
terms.definition: CD133-positive hematopoietic stem cell is a hematopoietic stem cell that is CD34-positive, CD90-positive, and CD133-positive.
terms.clComment: Cell markers are associated with human hematopoietic stem cells. Originally described in the dendritic cell ontology (DC_CL:0000035)(PMID:19243617).
terms.notes: Label says CD34-positive, CD38-negative, but the CL text definition begins 'CD133-positive hematopoietic stem cell is ...' and the EXACT synonym is 'CD133-positive hematopoietic stem cell'; the logical definition includes both CD34+ CD38- and CD133+ CD90+. Reported upstream-worthy inconsistency; recorded as published.

terms.label: myeloid leukocyte
terms.definition: A cell of the monocyte, granulocyte, or mast cell lineage.

terms.label: granulocyte
terms.definition: A leukocyte with abundant granules in the cytoplasm.

practice.comment: OMIP-101 gates granulocytes as CD66+ (clone B1.1) vs SSC-A. CL's own axiom uses CD66b (CEACAM8).

terms.notes: Logical definition includes CD66b+, CD11b+, CD87+ and CD3-, CD8a-, CD19-, CD56-.

terms.label: neutrophil
terms.definition: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte that in its mature form has a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes.

terms.label: eosinophil
terms.definition: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and which can be stained by the dye eosin. Eosinophils are CD9-positive, CD191-positive, and CD193-positive.
terms.clComment: Eosinophils are also CD14-negative, CD32-positive, CD44-positive, CD48-positive, CD69-positive, CD192-negative, MBP1-positive, MBP2-positive, TLR2-negative, TLR4-negative, and lineage-negative (B220, CD2, CD14, CD19, CD56, CD71, CD117, CD123, CD235a (glycophorin A), and TER119). The cytokines IL-3, IL-5, and GM-CSF are involved in their development and differentiation. Usually considered CD16-negative, CD16 is observed on eosinophilic metamyelocyte.

terms.label: basophil
terms.definition: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte that in its mature form has an irregularly shaped, pale-staining nucleus that is partially constricted into two lobes, and with cytoplasm that contains coarse, bluish-black granules of variable size. Basophils contain vasoactive amines such as histamine and serotonin, which are released on appropriate stimulation. A basophil is CD123-positive, CD193-positive, CD203c-positive, and FceRIa-positive.
terms.clComment: Matures in the bone marrow and account for <1% of leukocytes in the peripheral blood, spleen, and bone marrow. Basophils are described as being CD11a-positive, CD11b-positive, CD13-positive, CD15-positive, CD18-positive, CD21-positive, CD25-positive, CD29-positive, CD35-positive, CD40-positive, CD40L-positive, CD44-positive, CD45R-negative, CD46-positive, CD49a-positive, CD49b-positive, CD49d-positive, CD55-positive, CD59-positive, CD62L-positive, CD63-positive, CD69-positive, CD90-negative, CD116-positive, CD117-negative, CD124-positive, CD125-positive, CD131-positive, CD161-positive, CD184-positive, CD191-positive, CD192-positive, CD197-positive, CD200R3-positive, CD218-positive, CD282-positive, CD284-positive, CD289-positive, CD290-positive, CD294-positive, natural killer cell receptor 2B4-positive, smad1-positive, CD3-negative, CD4-negative, CD7-negative, CD8-negative, CD14-negative, CD15-negative, CD16-negative, CD19-negative, CD20-negative, CD34-negative, CD36-negative, CD45R-negative, CD56-negative, CD57-negative, CD235a-negative, and GR1-negative. Transcription factors- GATA1-positive, PU.1-positive.

practice.comment: OMIP-069 gates basophils from live singlets as CD45-intermediate CD123+ then HLA-DR- CD38+. CL axioms (CD123-high, CD193-high, CD203c+, FceRIa-high) agree on CD123.

terms.label: monocyte
terms.definition: Myeloid mononuclear recirculating leukocyte that can act as a precursor of tissue macrophages, osteoclasts and some populations of tissue dendritic cells.
terms.clComment: Morphology: Mononuclear cell, diameter, 14 to 20 _M, N/C ratio 2:1-1:1. Nucleus may appear in variety of shapes: round, kidney, lobulated, or convoluted. Fine azurophilic granules present; markers: CD11b (shared with other myeloid cells), human: CD14, mouse: F4/80-mid,GR1-low; location: Blood, but can be recruited into tissues; role or process: immune & tissue remodelling; lineage: hematopoietic, myeloid.

practice.comment: OMIP-101: CD33+ myeloid, CD3-CD19-CD56-, HLA-DR+, then CD14/CD16. OMIP-069: monocyte scatter gate, then CD14/CD16. CL's monocyte term has no marker axioms.

terms.label: CD14-positive monocyte
terms.definition: A monocyte that expresses CD14 and is negative for the lineage markers CD3, CD19, and CD20.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'monocyte'. Note that while CD14 is considered a reliable marker for human monocytes, it is only expressed on approximately 85% of mouse monocytes.

terms.label: classical monocyte
terms.definition: A monocyte that responds rapidly to microbial stimuli by secreting cytokines and antimicrobial factors and which is characterized by high expression of CCR2 in both rodents and humans, negative for the lineage markers CD3, CD19, and CD20, and of larger size than non-classical monocytes.
terms.clComment: Markers: CCR2+CXCCR1<low> (human, mouse, rat).

practice.comment: Classical monocytes: CD14+CD16- (OMIP-101/069); CD14hi CD16- (Maecker 2012). CL encodes CD14+CD16- only on the child term CL:0002057.

terms.label: CD14-positive, CD16-negative classical monocyte
terms.definition: A classical monocyte that is CD14-positive, CD16-negative, CD64-positive, CD163-positive.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'CD16- monocyte'. The markers used in the definition are associated with human monocytes.

terms.label: intermediate monocyte
terms.definition: A monocyte that has characteristics of both patrolling and inflammatory monocytes.

practice.comment: Intermediate monocytes: CD14+ CD16+/low. CL encodes CD14+CD16+ on CL:0002397 (CD14-positive, CD16-positive monocyte).

terms.label: CD14-positive, CD16-positive monocyte
terms.definition: A CD14-positive monocyte that is also CD16-positive and CCR2-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'CD16+ monocyte'. Markers are associated with human cells. Note that this cell type encompasses both human intermediate monocytes (CD14+, CD16-low), and human non-classical monocytes (CD14-low, CD16+).

terms.label: non-classical monocyte
terms.definition: A type of monocyte characterized by low expression of CCR2, low responsiveness to monocyte chemoattractant CCL2/MCP1, low phagocytic activity, and decrease size relative to classical monocytes, but increased co-stimulatory activity. May also play a role in tissue repair.
terms.clComment: Markers: CCR2-CX3CCR1+ (human, mouse, rat); human: CD16+, CCR5+, CD32/FcgRII-high, MHCII+, CD86+; mouse: CD62L-Ly6C-.

practice.comment: Non-classical monocytes: CD14-CD16+ (OMIP-101/069); CD14low CD16hi (Maecker 2012). CL encodes CD14-low CD16+ on CL:0002396.

terms.label: CD14-low, CD16-positive monocyte
terms.definition: A patrolling monocyte that is CD14-low and CD16-positive.
terms.clComment: Markers are associated with human monocytes.

terms.label: dendritic cell
terms.definition: A cell of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation. These cells are lineage negative (CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD34-negative, and CD56-negative).

practice.comment: Lineage-negative HLA-DR-high cells (Maecker 2012); OMIP-069 gates CD3-CD19-CD56-CD14- HLA-DR+.

terms.label: dendritic cell, human
terms.definition: A dendritic cell with the phenotype HLA-DRA-positive.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'dendritic cell'. The inclusion of HLA-DRA in the definition restricts this definition to human dendritic cells.

practice.comment: Same practical gate as dendritic cell.

terms.label: conventional dendritic cell
terms.definition: Conventional dendritic cell is a dendritic cell that is CD11c-high.
terms.clComment: Originally described in the dendritic cell ontology (DC_CL:0000003)(PMID:19243617) These cells are also CD20-negative, MHCII-positive.
terms.notes: CL's EXACT synonyms include 'DC1' and 'type 1 DC' (older nomenclature); these do not mean cDC1 (CD141+ XCR1+). Avoid synonym matching on 'DC1'.

terms.label: myeloid dendritic cell
terms.definition: A dendritic cell of the myeloid lineage.
terms.clComment: These cells are CD1a-negative, CD1b-positive, CD11a-positive, CD11c-positive, CD13-positive, CD14-negative, CD20-negative, CD21-negative, CD33-positive, CD40-negative, CD50-positive, CD54-positive, CD58-positive, CD68-negative, CD80-negative, CD83-negative, CD85j-positive, CD86-positive, CD89-negative, CD95-positive, CD120a-negative, CD120b-positive, CD123-negative, CD178-negative, CD206-negative, CD207-negative, CD209-negative, and TNF-alpha-negative. Upon TLR stimulation, they are capable of producing high levels of TNF-alpha, IL-6, CXCL8 (IL-8).

practice.comment: Myeloid DCs: Lin- HLA-DR+ CD11c+ (CD123-). OMIP-101 gates mDCs as CD14-CD16- HLA-DR+ CD11c+ within CD33+ myeloid cells.

terms.label: myeloid dendritic cell, human
terms.definition: A myeloid dendritic cell with the phenotype HLA-DRA-positive and CD14-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'myeloid dendritic cell'. The inclusion of HLA-DRA in the definition restricts this definition to human myeloid dendritic cells.

terms.label: CD1c-positive myeloid dendritic cell
terms.definition: A myeloid dendritic cell that is CD1c-positive.
terms.clComment: Normally represent 10-20% of peripheral blood mDCs (human). They are also CD281-positive (TLR1), CD282-positive (TLR2), CD283-positive (TLR3), CD284-positive (TLR4), CD285-positive (TLR5), CD286-positive (TLR6), CD288-positive (TLR8), and CD290-positive (TLR10) [PMID:20204387]. Upon TLR stimulation, these cells were potent producers of CXCL8 (IL-8), while producing little TNF-alpha.

terms.label: CD141-positive myeloid dendritic cell
terms.definition: A myeloid dendritic cell found in the blood, lymph nodes, tonsil, bone marrow, and spleen that is CD141-positive (BDCA-3), XCR1-positive, and Clec9A-positive. This cell-type can cross-present antigen to CD8-positive T cells and can produce inteferon-beta.
terms.clComment: Markers are found in human cells. Normally they represent 3-5% of peripheral blood mDCs (human). These cells express high levels of CD283 (TLR3), are capable of producing IL-12p70 and IFN-beta upon stimulation, and inducing a TH1 response [PMCID:PMC2882828]. They are also Necl2-positive. May be human equivalent of murine CD8-alpha-positive DCs.
terms.notes: In this CL release CD141-positive myeloid DC is asserted is_a both myeloid dendritic cell and plasmacytoid dendritic cell (CL:0000784). This looks like a modeling quirk; CytoWeave should not infer pDC from it.

terms.label: CD16-positive myeloid dendritic cell
terms.definition: A myeloid dendritic cell found in the blood that is CD16-positive.
terms.clComment: Normally represent 65-75% of peripheral blood mDCs (human). They are also CD281-positive (TLR1), CD282-positive (TLR2), CD284-positive (TLR4), CD285-positive (TLR5), CD286-positive (TLR6), CD288-positive (TLR8), CD289-positive (TLR9), and CD290-positive (TLR10) by RT-PCR [PMID:17332250]. Upon TLR stimulation, these cells are potent producers of TNF-alpha, while producing little CXCL8 (IL8).

terms.label: plasmacytoid dendritic cell
terms.definition: A dendritic cell type of distinct morphology, localization, and surface marker expression (CD123-positive) from other dendritic cell types and associated with early stage immune responses, particularly the release of physiologically abundant amounts of type I interferons in response to infection.

practice.comment: CL's generic pDC term has CD123 only in its text definition; the human term CL:0001058 encodes HLA-DR+ CD123+ CD11c- CD14-.

terms.notes: CL's EXACT synonyms include 'DC2' and 'type 2 DC' (older nomenclature for pDC); these do not mean cDC2 (CD1c+). Avoid synonym matching on 'DC2'.

terms.label: plasmacytoid dendritic cell, human
terms.definition: A plasmacytoid dendritic cell with the phenotype HLA-DRA-positive, CD123-positive, CD11c-negative, and CD14-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'plasmacytoid dendritic cell'. The inclusion of HLA-DRA in the definition restricts this definition to human plasmacytoid dendritic cells.

terms.label: lymphocyte
terms.definition: A lymphocyte is a leukocyte commonly found in the blood and lymph that has the characteristics of a large nucleus, a neutral staining cytoplasm, and prominent heterochromatin.
terms.clComment: Editors note: consider adding taxon constraint to vertebrata (PMID:18025161)

practice.comment: OMIP-069 gates lymphocytes on FSC-A/SSC-A; OMIP-101 defines them as CD33- SSC-low.

terms.label: T cell
terms.definition: A type of lymphocyte whose defining characteristic is the expression of a T cell receptor complex.

practice.comment: CL defines T cells by the TCR complex (GO:0042101 on CL:0002419); CD3 is the practical surrogate.

terms.label: mature T cell
terms.definition: A T cell that expresses a T cell receptor complex and has completed T cell selection.

terms.label: alpha-beta T cell
terms.definition: A T cell that expresses an alpha-beta T cell receptor complex.

practice.comment: Alpha-beta T cells are usually inferred as CD3+ TCRgd-; anti-TCRab is rarely on panels.

terms.label: mature alpha-beta T cell
terms.definition: A alpha-beta T cell that has a mature phenotype.

terms.label: gamma-delta T cell
terms.definition: A T cell that expresses a gamma-delta T cell receptor complex.
terms.clComment: Note that gamma-delta T cells have both thymic and extrathymic differentiation pathways.

terms.label: CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell
terms.definition: A mature alpha-beta T cell that expresses an alpha-beta T cell receptor and the CD4 coreceptor.

practice.comment: OMIP-101/069 gate CD4 T cells from CD3+ TCRgd- (and CD56-, MAIT-excluded in OMIP-101) cells.

terms.label: CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
terms.definition: A T cell expressing an alpha-beta T cell receptor and the CD8 coreceptor.

terms.label: naive T cell
terms.definition: Mature T cell not yet exposed to antigen with the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD45RA-positive, and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD62L-high and CD44-low.

practice.comment: Matches CL's own axioms; CD127+, CD62L-high, CD44-low in CL are not usually measured.

terms.notes: Logical definition includes CD45RA+, CCR7+, CD127+, CD62L-high, CD44-low.

terms.label: memory T cell
terms.definition: A long-lived, antigen-experienced T cell that has acquired a memory phenotype including distinct surface markers and the ability to differentiate into an effector T cell upon antigen reexposure.

practice.comment: No single gate; memory is the union of central memory, effector memory and TEMRA gates.

terms.label: naive thymus-derived CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell
synonyms: naive thymus-derived CD4-positive, alpha-beta T lymphocyte
terms.definition: An antigen inexperienced CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell with the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive and CD62L-positive. This cell type develops in the thymus. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD62L-high, and CD44-low.
terms.clComment: These cells have not been exposed to antigen following thymic T-cell selection; found in blood and secondary lymphoid organs. This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'naive CD4+ T cell', but includes additional markers known to be expressed on naive CD4+ T cells.

practice.comment: OMIP-069 additionally requires CD27+CD28+; OMIP-090 requires CD28+ and separates CD95+ stem cell memory cells.

terms.label: CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has differentiated into a memory T cell.

practice.comment: Approximation; CL's CD45RO-positive child (CL:0001204) is what CD45RO+ gates map to.

terms.label: CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell, CD45RO-positive
synonyms: CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T lymphocyte, CD45RO-positive
terms.definition: CD4-positive, alpha-beta long-lived T cell with the phenotype CD45RO-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative.

terms.label: central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell
synonyms: central CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell
central CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T lymphocyte
central memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T lymphocyte
terms.definition: CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell with the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'central memory CD4+ T cell', but includes additional markers known to be expressed on central memory CD4+ T cells.

practice.comment: CL additionally requires CD25- (own axiom) and CD45RO+ and CD127+ (inherited from CL:0001204); panels without CD45RO use CD45RA- as the surrogate.

terms.label: effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell
synonyms: effector CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell
effector CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T lymphocyte
effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T lymphocyte
terms.definition: CD4-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell with the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'effector memory CD4+ T cell', but includes additional markers known to be expressed on effector memory CD4+ T cells.

practice.comment: OMIP-069 subdivides CCR7-CD45RA- cells by CD27/CD28 into early, early-like, intermediate and terminal effectors instead of a single effector memory gate.

terms.label: effector memory CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell, terminally differentiated
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, alpha beta memory T cell with the phenotype CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, and CCR7-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is seen in human but not found in the mouse.

practice.comment: OMIP-069 further requires CD27-CD28- for CD8 'CD45RA terminal effector'; OMIP-090 requires CD28- for TEMRA.

terms.label: effector memory CD45RA-positive, alpha-beta T cell, terminally differentiated
synonyms: terminally differentiated effector memory CD45RA+ T cells
terminally differentiated effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA
terms.definition: An alpha-beta memory T cell with the phenotype CD45RA-positive.

practice.comment: Maecker 2012 calls CCR7-CD45RA+ cells 'effector T cells'; OMIP-101 calls them terminally differentiated effector memory. CL has no marker axioms on this term in OBO (text definition: CD45RA+).

terms.notes: No marker restrictions in the OBO file; the CD45RA+ phenotype is only in the text definition. The CD4 and CD8 TEMRA children carry CD45RA+, CD45RO-, CCR7- axioms.

terms.label: naive thymus-derived CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
synonyms: naive thymus-dervied CD8-positive, alpha-beta T lymphocyte
terms.definition: A CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has not experienced activation via antigen contact and has the phenotype CD45RA-positive, CCR7-positive and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD62L-high and CD44-low.
terms.clComment: This cell traffics in secondary lymphoid organs and blood.  This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'naive CD8+ T cell', but includes additional markers known to be expressed on naive CD8+ T cells.

terms.label: CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell
terms.definition: A CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has differentiated into a memory T cell.

practice.comment: Approximation; see CL:0001203 for CD45RO+ gates.

terms.label: CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell, CD45RO-positive
synonyms: CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T lymphocyte, CD45RO-positive
terms.definition: A CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell with memory phenotype indicated by being CD45RO and CD127-positive. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative.

terms.label: central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
synonyms: central CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell
central CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T lymphocyte
central memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T lymphocyte
terms.definition: CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell with the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'central memory CD8+ T cell', but includes additional markers known to be expressed on central memory CD8+ T cells.

practice.comment: As for CD4 central memory: CL also requires CD25- (own axiom) and CD45RO+, CD127+ (inherited from CL:0001203).

terms.label: effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
synonyms: effector CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell
effector CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T lymphocyte
effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T lymphocyte
terms.definition: CD8-positive, alpha-beta memory T cell with the phenotype CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'effector memory CD8+ T cell', but includes additional markers known to be expressed on effector memory CD8+ T cells.

terms.label: effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell, terminally differentiated
terms.definition: A CD8-positive, alpha beta memory T cell with the phenotype CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, and CCR7-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is seen in human but not found in the mouse.

terms.label: regulatory T cell
terms.definition: A T cell which regulates overall immune responses as well as the responses of other T cell subsets through direct cell-cell contact and cytokine release.
terms.clComment: This cell type may express FoxP3 and CD25 and secretes IL-10 and TGF-beta.
terms.notes: Generic regulatory T cell; no marker axioms.

terms.label: CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell
synonyms: CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T lymphocyte
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta T cell that regulates overall immune responses as well as the responses of other T cell subsets through direct cell-cell contact and cytokine release.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'Treg'.  The inclusion of CD127lo in the logical definition is compatible with both human and mouse T cells of this subtype.

practice.comment: Matches CL's axioms (CD25+, CD127-low). FOXP3 is not in CL's axioms and not on these panels.

terms.notes: Treg variants in CL: CL:0000792 is the CD4+CD25+ Treg (CD25+, CD127-low). CL also has CCR4+ Treg subsets (CL:0001047, CL:0001045, CL:0001046) and CD8+ Tregs (CL:0000795, CL:0000919), not included here.

terms.label: naive regulatory T cell
terms.definition: A regulatory T cell that has not encountered antigen.
terms.clComment: This cell type has been described as CD45RA-negative, but this doesn't fit with our current definition of naive T cell.

practice.comment: Naive Treg = CD45RA+ Treg (OMIP-090 panel C; Miyara population I = CD45RA+ CD25+).

terms.label: memory regulatory T cell
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, CD25-positive alpha-beta regulatory T cell that has encountered antigen.
terms.clComment: Cell has been described as being CD45RA-positive in human, but this doesn't fit with our current definition memory T cell.

practice.comment: OMIP-090 calls CD45RA- CXCR5- Tregs 'memory Treg' and CD45RA- CXCR5+ 'TFR'.

terms.label: CD4-positive helper T cell
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that cooperates with other lymphocytes via direct contact or cytokine release to initiate a variety of immune functions.

terms.label: T follicular helper cell
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, CXCR5-positive, CCR7-negative alpha-beta T cell located in follicles of secondary lymph nodes that is BCL6-high, ICOS-high and PD1-high, and stimulates follicular B cells to undergo class-switching and antibody production.

practice.comment: Circulating Tfh-like cells in blood. CL's term describes follicular Tfh in lymphoid tissue (CCR7-, PD-1-high, ICOS-high, BCL6-high); OMIP-069 gates blood Tfh as CD45RA-CCR7+CXCR5+. Mapping blood cTfh to CL:0002038 is an approximation.

terms.notes: In this CL release Tfh is also is_a 'CD4-positive exhausted alpha-beta T cell' (CL:0020030). Recorded as published.

terms.label: T-helper 1 cell
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has the phenotype T-bet-positive, CXCR3-positive, CCR6-negative, and is capable of producing interferon-gamma.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'Th1 CD4+ T cell', but its logical definition includes additional known characteristics of T-helper 1 T cells.
terms.notes: Defined by T-bet (intracellular), CXCR3+, CCR6-. Not expressible on either CytoWeave example panel (no CXCR3/CCR6).

terms.label: T-helper 2 cell
terms.definition: A CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has the phenotype GATA-3-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-negative, and is capable of producing interleukin-4.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'non-Th1/Th17 CD4+ T cell' (see CL:0001051), but includes the additional necessary and sufficient conditions to allow classification as a T-helper 2 T cell.
terms.notes: Defined by GATA3 (intracellular), CXCR3-, CCR6-. Not expressible on either example panel.

terms.label: T-helper 17 cell
terms.definition: CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell with the phenotype RORgamma-t-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-positive, and capable of producing IL-17.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'Th17 CD4+ T cell', but its logical definition includes additional known characteristics of T-helper 17 T cells.
terms.notes: Defined by RORgt (intracellular), CXCR3-, CCR6+. Not expressible on either example panel.

terms.label: mucosal-associated invariant T cell
terms.definition: An alpha-beta T cell that is found in the lamina propria of mucosal tissues and is restricted by the MR-1 molecule. This cell develops from double-positive, alpha-beta thymocyte.
terms.notes: Generic MAIT term has no marker axioms; use the human term CL:0020002 (TRAV1-2+, CD161-high) when Va7.2 is measured.

terms.label: mucosal-associated invariant T cell, human
terms.definition: A mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cell found in various tissues including human blood, liver, gut, and lung, characterised by a semi-invariant T cell receptor (TCR) comprising TRAV1-2 (Vα7.2) predominantly paired with TRAJ33, and high expression of CD161. Upon activation, MAIT cells produce inflammatory cytokines, including IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-17.

practice.comment: Matches CL's axioms. Neither CytoWeave example panel has TRAV1-2 (Va7.2); CD161-high CD8 T cells alone are not specific.

terms.notes: Asserted is_a both MAIT and mature NK T cell (CL:0000814).

terms.label: mature NK T cell
terms.definition: A mature alpha-beta T cell of a distinct lineage that bears natural killer markers and a T cell receptor specific for a limited set of ligands. NK T cells have activation and regulatory roles particularly early in an immune response.

practice.comment: Both OMIPs call CD3+CD56+ cells 'NKT-like', not NKT. CL's NK T cell is a distinct lineage with a restricted TCR (CD1d-restricted iNKT in practice). Suggest with low confidence.

terms.notes: CD161 is referenced via PR:000001874 (KLRB1-like protein gene family).

terms.label: mature NK T cell, human
synonyms: mature natural killer T cell, human
mature natural killer T lymphocyte, human
terms.definition: A mature NK T cell that can be identified by the expression of CD56 in humans.

practice.comment: CL's human NK T cell term is defined by CD56 expression, so CD3+CD56+ 'NKT-like' cells fit its axioms, but the parent term implies an invariant TCR. Confirm with the user.

terms.label: double-positive, alpha-beta thymocyte
terms.definition: A thymocyte expressing the alpha-beta T cell receptor complex as well as both the CD4 and CD8 coreceptors.
terms.clComment: Thymocytes of this stage are undergoing positive and negative selection.
terms.notes: Thymocyte term (logical definition includes part_of thymus). CL (2026-06-08) has no term for peripheral CD4+CD8+ T cells; for a blood CD3+CD4+CD8+ gate suggest CL:0000791 or CL:0000084 instead.

terms.label: double negative thymocyte
terms.definition: A thymocyte that lacks expression of CD4 and CD8.
terms.clComment: These are precursors to mature T cells; normally, they do not circulate, but are found in the thymus and they have not undergone rearrangement of the alpha and beta T cell receptor genes.
terms.notes: Thymocyte term. Its EXACT synonyms 'double negative T cell' and 'CD4-CD8- T cell' are misleading for peripheral blood: CL (2026-06-08) has no term for peripheral CD4-CD8- alpha-beta T cells. For a blood CD3+CD4-CD8- gate suggest CL:0000791 (mature alpha-beta T cell) or CL:0000084 (T cell), not this term.

terms.label: B cell
terms.definition: A lymphocyte of B lineage that is capable of B cell mediated immunity.

practice.comment: Maecker 2012 recommends CD19 as the parent B-cell marker because plasmablasts are CD20-low/negative.

terms.label: B cell, CD19-positive
terms.definition: A B cell that is CD19-positive.

terms.label: mature B cell
terms.definition: A B cell that is mature, having left the bone marrow. Initially, these cells are IgM-positive and IgD-positive, and they can be activated by antigen.
terms.clComment: Mature B cells are also reportedly CD10-negative, CD19-positive, CD22-positive, CD34-negative, CD48-positive, CD79a-positive, CD84-positive, CD127-negative, CD352-positive, RAG-negative, TdT-negative, Vpre-B-negative, and pre-BCR-negative. Transcription factors expressed: Pax5-positive.

practice.comment: No specific mature-B gate; non-transitional, non-plasmablast CD19+ cells.

terms.label: naive B cell
terms.definition: A naive B cell is a mature B cell that has the phenotype surface IgD-positive, surface IgM-positive, CD20-positive, CD27-negative and that has not yet been activated by antigen in the periphery.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'naive B cell'. Per DSD: Naive B cells are also reportedly CD10-negative, CD19-positive, CD20-positive, CD21-positive, CD22-positive, CD25-negative, CD27-negative, CD34-negative, CD40-positive, CD43-negative, CD45-positive, CD48-positive, CD53-positive, CD80-negative, CD81-positive, CD84-positive, CD86-negative, CD95-negative, CD138-negative, CD150-positive, CD184/CXCR4-positive, CD185/CXCR5-positive, CD196/CCR6-positive, CD200-positive, CD229-positive, CD243-positive, CD289-positive, CD290-positive, CD352-positive, MHCII/HLA-DR-positive, cadherin 9-positive, and sIgH-positive, Transcription factors: Pax5-positive, ETS1-positive, FOXO1A-positive, KLF4-positive, KLF9-positive, MiTF-positive, OBF1-positive, PLZF-positive, and SpiB-positive.

practice.comment: Matches CL axioms (IgD+, IgM+, CD20+, CD27-). Transitional cells (CD24hi CD38hi) fall in this gate unless excluded.

terms.label: transitional stage B cell
terms.definition: An immature B cell of an intermediate stage between the pre-B cell stage and the mature naive stage with the phenotype surface IgM-positive and CD19-positive, and are subject to the process of B cell selection. A transitional B cell migrates from the bone marrow into the peripheral circulation, and then to the spleen.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'transitional B cell'.

practice.comment: Matches CL axioms (CD24-high, CD38-high, IgM+, CD20+).

terms.label: memory B cell
terms.definition: A memory B cell is a mature B cell that is long-lived, readily activated upon re-encounter of its antigenic determinant, and has been selected for expression of higher affinity immunoglobulin. This cell type has the phenotype CD19-positive, CD20-positive, MHC Class II-positive, and CD138-negative.
terms.clComment: Memory B-cells are also reportedly CD5-negative, CD10-negative, CD21-positive, CD22-positive, CD23-negative, CD24-positive, CD25-positive, CD27-positive, CD34-negative, CD38-negative, CD40-positive, CD43-negative, CD44-positive, CD45-positive, CD53-positive, CD80-negative, CD81-negative, CD86-positive, and CD196/CCR6-positive.

practice.comment: Maecker 2012: CD27 separates naive (CD27-) from memory (CD27+) B cells. CL's memory B term does not use CD27 (CD27- double-negative memory B cells exist).

terms.label: unswitched memory B cell
terms.definition: An unswitched memory B cell is a memory B cell that has the phenotype IgM-positive, IgD-positive, CD27-positive, CD138-negative, IgG-negative, IgE-negative, and IgA-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'IgD+ memory B cell'. Per DSD: Unswitched memory B cells are also reportedly CD48-positive, CD84-positive, CD229-positive, and CD352-positive.

practice.comment: OMIP-069 gates IgD+CD27+ B cells (labeled 'IgD+ CD27+ B cells'). Matches CL's IgD+ CD27+ axioms.

terms.label: class switched memory B cell
terms.definition: A class switched memory B cell is a memory B cell that has undergone Ig class switching and therefore is IgM-negative on the cell surface. These cells are CD27-positive and have either IgG, IgE, or IgA on the cell surface.
terms.clComment: Per DSD: Class switched memory B cells are also reportedly CD48-positive, CD229-positive, and CD352-positive.

practice.comment: As for CL:4052108; CL also requires IgM- (not on the example panels).

terms.label: IgD-negative memory B cell
terms.definition: A memory B cell that lacks expression of surface IgD.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'IgD- memory B cell'.  The majority of these cells are class-switched, though some are IgM-positive.

practice.comment: OMIP-069: IgD- B cells, then CD20+ = IgD- memory (CD20- = plasmablasts).

terms.label: IgD-negative class switched memory B cell
terms.definition: A class switched memory B cell that lacks IgD on the cell surface.

practice.comment: OMIP-101 'memory' gate is IgD-CD27+. Class switching (IgG/IgA/IgE+) is assumed, not measured, unless isotype markers are present.

terms.label: double negative memory B cell
terms.definition: A memory B cell with the phenotype IgD-negative and CD27-negative.

practice.comment: Matches CL axioms. OMIP-069 does not gate this population separately (its IgD- gate is CD27+/-).

terms.notes: Logical definition is memory B cell + IgD- + CD27-; its asserted is_a parent is IgD-negative memory B cell.

terms.label: antibody secreting cell
terms.definition: A lymphocyte of B lineage that is devoted to secreting large amounts of immunoglobulin.

terms.label: plasmablast
terms.definition: An activated mature (naive or memory) B cell that is secreting immunoglobulin, typified by being CD27-positive, CD38-positive, CD138-negative.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'plasmablast'. Plasmablasts are also reportedly CD48-positive, CD63-positive, CD229-positive, CD270-positive, CD319-positive, CD352-positive, CD361-positive, and IgD-negative.

practice.comment: Matches CL axioms (CD27-high, CD38-high, CD20-, CD138-).

terms.label: plasma cell
terms.definition: A terminally differentiated, post-mitotic, antibody secreting cell of the B cell lineage with the phenotype CD138-positive, surface immunonoglobulin-negative, and MHC Class II-negative. Plasma cells are oval or round with extensive rough endoplasmic reticulum, a well-developed Golgi apparatus, and a round nucleus having a characteristic cartwheel heterochromatin pattern and are devoted to producing large amounts of immunoglobulin.
terms.clComment: Plasma cells develop in the spleen and migrate to the bone marrow. Plasma cells are also reportedly CD5-negative, CD10-negative, CD19-positive, CD20-negative, CD21-negative, CD22-negative, CD23-negative, CD24-negative, CD25-negative, CD27-positive, CD34-negative, CD38-positive, CD40-positive, CD43-positive, CD45-positive, CD48-positive, CD53-low, CD80-negative, CD81-positive, CD86-positive, CD95-positive, CD196-negative, CD229-positive, CD270-positive, CD352-positive, CD361-positive, and IgD-negative. Transcription factors: BLIMP1-positive, IRF4-positive, PAX5-negative, SpiB-negative, Ets1-negative, and XBP1-positive.

terms.label: innate lymphoid cell
terms.definition: A lymphocyte that lacks characteristic T cell, B cell, myeloid cell, and dendritic cell markers, that functions as part of the innate immune response to produce cytokines and other effector responses.

practice.comment: Total ILCs as lineage-negative CD127+ (OMIP-101 excludes CD3/CD4/CD19/CD16/CD56; OMIP-069 excludes CD3/CD19/CD20/CD14/CD123 and HLA-DR+).

terms.label: natural killer cell
terms.definition: A lymphocyte that can spontaneously kill a variety of target cells without prior antigenic activation via germline encoded activation receptors and also regulate immune responses via cytokine release and direct contact with other cells.

practice.comment: OMIP-101 excludes CD3, CD4 and CD19; OMIP-069 gates CD3- TCRgd- HLA-DR- then CD56/CD16.

terms.label: CD16-negative, CD56-bright natural killer cell, human
synonyms: CD56-bright cytokine secreting natural killer cell
terms.definition: NK cell that has the phenotype CD56-bright, CD16-negative, and CD84-positive with the function to secrete interferon-gamma but is not cytotoxic.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'CD16-CD56bright NK cell'. Markers are associated with human cell types.

practice.comment: Matches CL axioms (CD56-high, CD16-, HLA-DR-, CD84+). Note: Maecker 2012 describes the minor subset as CD16+CD56hi, which differs from CL's CD16-negative definition.

terms.notes: Human-specific term (taxon constraint Homo sapiens).

terms.label: CD16-positive, CD56-dim natural killer cell, human
terms.definition: A mature natural killer cell that has the phenotype CD56-low, CD16-positive and which is capable of cytotoxicity and cytokine production.
terms.clComment: This cell type is compatible with the HIPC Lyoplate markers for 'CD16+CD56+ NK cell'. Markers are associated with human cell types.

practice.comment: Matches CL axioms (CD56-low, CD16+, HLA-DR-). OMIP-069 calls CD56+CD16+ cells 'mature NK'.

terms.notes: Human-specific term (taxon constraint Homo sapiens).

terms.label: group 2 innate lymphoid cell, human
terms.definition: A group 2 innate lymphoid cell in the human with the phenotype CD25-positive, CD127-positive, CD161-positive, and GATA-3-positive.
terms.notes: Defined by CD294 (CRTH2)+, CD25+, CD127+, CD161+ and GATA3. The mass cytometry example panel has CD294, CD25, CD127 and CD161.
